evidence: Jetz & Pyron 2018 SI: 15 calibrations; the root (Amphibia-Amniota, 330.4-350.1 Ma, pruned with Homo by D7), Batrachia (245-330.4 Ma), Caudata (minimum 150.8 Ma) and twelve internal minima. None is on crown Lissamphibia.
parent_evidence: Jetz & Pyron 2018 SI, 'Backbone Matrix and Molecular Dating': the node above crown Lissamphibia is the root (Amphibia-Amniota, outgroup Homo sapiens, pruned by D7), 'constrained between 330.4-350.1Ma' (uniform); the node below on the Batrachia side carries a minimum of 245 Ma with a maximum of 330.4 Ma ('For the three non-sirenoid salamander calibrations and the MRCA of Batrachia, the maximum age was set to 330.4Ma, the minimum age of the root'). The crown lies between two two-sided calibrations, on the root and on Batrachia.
child_evidence: Jetz & Pyron 2018 SI, 'Backbone Matrix and Molecular Dating': the node below crown Lissamphibia on the Batrachia side, crown Batrachia, carries a minimum of 245 Ma and a maximum of 330.4 Ma ('For the three non-sirenoid salamander calibrations and the MRCA of Batrachia, the maximum age was set to 330.4Ma, the minimum age of the root'); every other calibration below the crown (Caudata 150.8 Ma and twelve internal minima) is younger than 245 Ma.
band_evidence: The crown is older than crown Batrachia, whose calibration minimum is 245 Ma, and younger than the root, whose uniform prior ends at 350.1 Ma: the calibrations on the nodes directly below and above confine crown Lissamphibia to 245-350.1 Ma.

prior_form: lognormal root-age density between a hard minimum of 333.56 Ma and a soft maximum of 422.4 Ma, midpoint 377.98 Ma; the 10,000 trees are dated under root ages drawn from it
evidence: Stein et al. 2018 accepted manuscript p.16: the root calibration is a lognormal density between a hard minimum of 333.56 Myr and a soft maximum of 422.4 Myr with its midpoint at 377.98 Myr; pp.16-18: 500 treePL datings of one fixed topology under root ages drawn from that density. The interval is set by the calibration by construction (D29), whatever its containment. Both dating scenarios (1 and 10 calibration fossils, accepted MS p.17) draw the 500 root ages from this density; the 10-fossil scenario, the one the source designates (SI p.2 l.26-28; D46), adds hard minima on 9 internal nodes, none on the root. No BEAST or treePL input file specifying the density is archived (VertLife distributes the tree sets only; BEAST was used only for prior-only taxon addition, MS p.18), so the range is quoted from the accepted manuscript. Root heights over 10.cal.tree.nex: median 377.83 Ma, central 95% 353.57-437.61, range 348.76-488.29 (the 'root age of 349 - 488 MYA' of SI p.2).
